reference: GNU coreutils cp invoked by system Bash with its standard executable PATH; expected command status, output bytes, and file tree are compared against the bash-os cp builtin.
coverage: Binary regular-file copy, source preservation, and verbose output
Multiple operands into an existing directory, including a leading-dash name after --
Recursive tree copy with a relative symlink
Archive copy preserving hard-link relationships, symlinks, and modes
Default following of a destination symlink including -f following an openable referent
Same-file and missing-source diagnostics with unchanged fixture data
Interactive overwrite acceptance and decline using bounded here-string input
Bash type/help metadata contract for the registered cp builtin
Additional bounded regular-file, hardlink, symlink and multi-operand error continuation regressions.
GNU --parents path retention, parent modes, archive links, and failure continuation.

GNU long options and -u/-l/-s/-b/-S/-T/-x/-d, --preserve/--no-preserve lists, --update=WHEN, --backup=CONTROL, --remove-destination, --attributes-only, --sparse and --reflink (guest compatibility pass 1).
exclusions: Device nodes, FIFOs, sockets, ACLs, extended attributes, and security labels are outside this private regular-file/symlink fixture suite.
The suite does not claim full GNU option coverage or compare timestamps because the harness tree snapshot records contents, modes, and link relationships but not timestamps.

Named-entry ACL behaviour added in guest compatibility pass 1 (ACL preservation by -p/-a, including a directory's default ACL) needs mapped IDs that this sandbox lacks (EINVAL for both arms); bashy-box's image smoke acl-42 checks it as root in the VM.

cases.purpose: Copies deterministic binary data, leaves the source intact, and compares GNU-compatible -v output.
cases.script:
printf 'head\000middle\377tail\n' > source
if cp -v source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]
printf 'cp-status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Copies multiple files into an existing directory and honors -- before a source whose name begins with a dash.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf 'dash-name\n' > ./-first
printf 'second\n' > second
if cp -- -first second destination; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Copies a nested directory recursively and preserves a relative symlink as a symlink.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub
printf 'nested payload\n' > source/sub/item
ln -s sub/item source/shortcut
if cp -R source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Checks -a over a directory containing a hard-linked pair and a symlink; the tree comparison includes modes and hard-link identity.
cases.script:
mkdir source
printf 'shared bytes\n' > source/one
ln source/one source/two
ln -s one source/shortcut
if cp -a source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Uses a controlled umask to make a 0640 source and verifies that -p preserves its mode and bytes.
cases.script:
umask 027
printf 'mode payload\n' > source
umask 022
if cp -p source copied; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Verifies -f does not override -n in either option order and checks the documented --no-clobber spelling.
cases.script:
printf 'new data\n' > source
printf 'first old\n' > first
printf 'second old\n' > second
printf 'third old\n' > third
if cp -fn source first && cp -nf source second && cp --no-clobber source third; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Checks the default behavior when a regular-file destination is a symlink: the target contents change and the symlink remains.
cases.script:
printf 'replacement\n' > source
printf 'old target\n' > target
ln -s target alias
if cp source alias; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: GNU cp -f follows an openable destination symlink and writes its referent while preserving the symlink.
cases.script:
printf 'replacement\n' > source
printf 'old target\n' > target
ln -s target alias
if cp -f source alias; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]]

cases.purpose: Captures same-file and missing-source failures and verifies that both the source and an existing destination remain unchanged; diagnostic wording may vary.
cases.script:
printf 'keep these bytes\n' > source
printf 'keep destination\n' > destination
if cp source source; then same_status=0; else same_status=$?; fi
if cp absent destination; then missing_status=0; else missing_status=$?; fi
printf 'same=%s missing=%s\n' "$same_status" "$missing_status"
[[ $same_status -eq 1 && $missing_status -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Exercises -i with deterministic no and yes answers; output and the resulting files are compared with GNU cp.
cases.script:
printf 'new data\n' > source
printf 'keep on decline\n' > declined
printf 'old before accept\n' > accepted
if cp -i source declined <<< n; then declined_status=0; else declined_status=$?; fi
if cp -i source accepted <<< y; then accepted_status=0; else accepted_status=$?; fi
printf 'declined-status=%s accepted-status=%s\n' "$declined_status" "$accepted_status"

cases.purpose: Checks Bash metadata only: cp is registered as a builtin and help exposes the documented synopsis. This does not count as cp operation coverage.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t cp) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help_text=$(help cp) || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *'Copy files and directories.'* && $help_text == *'bashcp [-abdfilnprRsTuvx] [-HLP] [-S SUFFIX] SOURCE... DEST'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'type=builtin\nhelp=cp synopsis present\n'

cases.purpose: GNU cp can write regular-file data to special destinations, but this suite is restricted to relative private fixture paths.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a synthetic writable special-file sink and isolated reader, or a reviewed syscall mock. This runner must not exercise host or raw device paths.

cases.purpose: Force should write an openable destination inode, preserving its other hardlinks and existing mode.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
chmod 600 target
ln target alias
cp -f source target

cases.purpose: A forced destination symlink to the source must fail without replacing either entry.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln -s source alias
cp -f source alias

cases.purpose: Both ordinary and forced copy should reject a dangling destination symlink without creating its target.
cases.script:
printf new > source
ln -s absent alias
if cp source alias; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if cp -f source alias; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"
[[ $a == 1 && $b == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: An unwritable destination is replaced after its write-open fails; its old hardlink keeps its data.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
ln target alias
chmod 400 target
cp -f source target

cases.purpose: Check source-read failure before forced replacement for regular and symlink destinations; restore source mode for snapshots.
cases.script:
printf secret > source
printf old > target
ln -s target alias
chmod 000 source
if cp -f source target; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if cp -f source alias; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
chmod 600 source
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"
[[ $a == 1 && $b == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: A missing middle operand must not prevent the later regular file from being copied.
cases.script:
mkdir destination
printf first > first
printf last > last
cp first absent last destination

cases.purpose: Compare default, -P, -H, and -L copying of a command-line source symlink using GNU as the oracle.
cases.script:
printf data > source
ln -s source alias
cp alias ordinary
cp -P alias physical
cp -H alias args
cp -L alias logical

cases.purpose: Reject copying between hardlink aliases while no-clobber still skips them successfully.
cases.script:
printf keep > source
ln source alias
if cp -f source alias; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
cp -n source alias
printf '%s\n' "$a"
[[ $a == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: If opening the destination referent fails, force may replace the symlink after the source is readable; its old referent stays intact.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > target
chmod 400 target
ln -s target alias
cp -f source alias

cases.purpose: Preserve archive behavior on preexisting hardlinked destinations, with and without force.
cases.script:
printf new > source
printf old > first
ln first first-alias
printf old > second
ln second second-alias
cp -a source first
cp -af source second

cases.purpose: Retain nested source names and create missing destination parents, including a trailing slash on the destination.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested destination
printf 'Hello, world!\n' > source/nested/message.txt
cp -v --parents source/nested/message.txt destination/
cat destination/source/nested/message.txt

cases.purpose: Preserve hard links and symlinks across --parents archive operands.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub destination
printf payload > source/sub/file
ln source/sub/file source/sub/hard
ln -s file source/sub/link
cp -a --parents source/sub/file source/sub/hard source/sub/link destination

cases.purpose: Populate newly created read-only parents before restoring source-derived modes under umask.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub destination
printf payload > source/sub/file
chmod 751 source
chmod 511 source/sub
umask 027
cp --parents source/sub/file destination

cases.purpose: Preserve preexisting destination parent modes even when -p is requested.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub destination/source/sub
printf payload > source/sub/file
chmod 700 destination/source destination/source/sub
cp -p --parents source/sub/file destination

cases.purpose: Reject a missing parent and still copy a later valid operand.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub destination
printf payload > source/sub/file
if cp --parents missing/sub/file source/sub/file destination; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Reject an absent or regular-file destination without changing it.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub
printf payload > source/sub/file
printf keep > destination
if cp --parents source/sub/file destination; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if cp --parents source/sub/file absent; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"
[[ $a == 1 && $b == 1 && ! -e absent ]]

cases.purpose: Copies each source into an existing directory using a grouped short option and attached argument.
cases.script:
mkdir dest
printf one > a; printf two > b
cp a -vtdest b

cases.purpose: Accepts the long forms and treats leading-dash operands literally after --.
cases.script:
mkdir dest
: > ./-a; : > b
cp --target-directory=dest -- -a && cp --target-directory dest b

cases.purpose: Rejects a regular file as an explicit target and leaves its contents intact.
cases.script:
printf one > a; printf before > dest
cp -t dest a

cases.purpose: Rejects multiple targets before copying.
cases.script:
mkdir x y; : > a
cp -tx -t y a

cases.purpose: --archive, --preserve[=LIST] and --no-preserve=mode keep or drop modes like GNU (guest pass 1).
cases.script:
mkdir d; printf a > d/f; chmod 640 d/f; ln -s f d/l
cp --archive d e
cp --preserve=mode d/f m
cp --preserve d/f p
cp -a --no-preserve=mode d/f nm
cp --preserve=mode,timestamps d/f mt
cp --preserve=bogus d/f x || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -u/--update[=older|all|none] keep a destination that is not older than the source.
cases.script:
printf new > s; printf old > d; touch -t 200101010000 d
cp -u s d; cat d; echo
printf keep > d; touch -t 203001010000 d
cp --update s d; cat d; echo
cp --update=none s d; cat d; echo
cp --update=all s d; cat d; echo
cp --update=bogus s d || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -l, -s and -rl make hard and symbolic links; -l follows source symlinks like GNU. Re-linking onto an existing hard link to the same file succeeds silently.
cases.script:
printf a > f; mkdir d; printf b > d/x; ln -s x d/y
cp -l f h
cp --link f h2
cp -s f s
cp --symbolic-link f s2
cp -rl d e
cp -l f h
cp -s f sub/s 2>/dev/null || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -b, --backup=CONTROL, -S/--suffix and -v report and keep backups like GNU.
cases.script:
printf 1 > f; printf 0 > o
cp -b f o
printf 2 > f; cp --backup=numbered f o
printf 3 > f; cp --backup=numbered f o
printf 4 > f; cp --backup=existing f o
printf 5 > f; cp -S .bak -b f o
printf 6 > f; cp -vb --suffix=.old f o
ls
cp --backup=bogus f o || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -T/--no-target-directory copies onto the named path instead of into it.
cases.script:
mkdir d e; printf a > d/f
cp -rT d e
cp --no-target-directory d/f g
cp -T d/f g h || echo rc=$?
cp -T -t e d/f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: --remove-destination unlinks first (breaking hard links); --attributes-only copies only metadata.
cases.script:
printf new > s; chmod 600 s; printf old > d; ln d dl
cp --remove-destination s d
cat d dl; echo
printf keep > k
cp --attributes-only -p s k
cat k; echo

cases.purpose: Sparse sources stay sparse, --sparse=never writes data, and --reflink=auto, -x and -d are accepted.
cases.script:
truncate -s 1M sp; printf x >> sp
cp sp c1; cp --sparse=always sp c2; cp --sparse=never sp c3
for f in c1 c2 c3; do b=$(du -k $f); b=${b%%[[:space:]]*}; if [ $b -lt 100 ]; then echo $f sparse; else echo $f dense; fi; done
cp --reflink=auto c1 r; cp --reflink=never c1 r2
mkdir d; ln -s ../c1 d/l; cp -rx d x; cp -rd d y
cp --sparse=bogus sp z || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: An unknown long option fails with status 1 instead of 2.
cases.script:
printf a > f
cp --bogus f g
